hypothesis: A small deterministic lifecycle-candidate boundary can prevent stale-generation resume, terminal-child resume, identity-rewriting replacement and over-budget nested spawn without acquiring execution authority.
counterhypothesis: Lifecycle state may accidentally become a second execution/child identity authority or may admit transitions that exceed the already-bound NativeChildRequest depth/generation evidence.
discriminator: Exact-type/content-bound predecessor revalidation plus deterministic negative tests for stale generation, illegal terminal resume, replacement identity reuse, generation ceiling and both policy/request nested-depth ceilings.
changes: added immutable ChildLifecyclePolicy with canonical JSON integer-domain validation
added immutable ChildLifecycleCandidate bound to exact NativeChildRequest identity/digest
RESUME requires explicit WAITING and carries neither replacement identity nor nested depth
REPLACE requires exactly next generation plus an explicit different replacement binding identity
NESTED_SPAWN rejects terminal state and must satisfy both lifecycle policy and NativeChildRequest max_nested_depth
consumer verifier reconstructs canonical content and checks lifecycle identity/digest/operation/generation
added deterministic fail-closed test suite and repository-hosted GitHub Actions workflow
non_credit: no target-runtime or VPS execution evidence
next_exact_action: Open a PR against current main and use the merge-ref repository-hosted CI as the dependency-compatibility discriminator. Do not terminally accept WP604 until exact CI evidence is green.
